notes: The request is one window action changing both axes; the observed NAWS sequence is recorded and not assumed atomic.
The observed 62-character row/scroll are post-write results. Whether clipping/materialization happened at resize, CUP, or the write is not observed.
The sequential #308 sample had no equivalent follow-up write, so the two samples cannot adjudicate a dual-axis vs sequential resize clipping difference.
No original pre-write body endpoint exists; pre-write full-row retention is only the TermForge engineering invariant asserted by the core replay.

limitations: One fixed 75 B ASCII direct-Telnet sample; main screen only; no alternate frame, Unicode, other sizes/orders, continuous output, selection/Find, full grid/style, ConPTY transport, physical presentation or performance.
The only post-resize body endpoint includes the fixed CUP+write; clipping/materialization attribution between resize, CUP and write remains unknown. There is no original pre-write body observation.
The observed original had scroll=5 and a written row of 62 characters; no internal history-row count or general scroll model is inferred.
The sequential width-then-height sample is not a comparable control for this write-intervened sample; no dual-axis vs sequential resize cropping conclusion is drawn.
The one NAWS event count/order is recorded for this run only; a single window request is not assumed to be an atomic two-axis transport event in general.
The old six-stage B/CD native-sync failure is not explained by this WindTerm UI observation and is not relaxed; ConPTY native-grid reflow after a simultaneous change remains unobserved.
The product retained-body direction remains the confirmed direction; this record is an original observation with a post-write endpoint, not a claim of WindTerm equality.
